summary: Tested the Fechamento (closure) feature end-to-end. Backend: new test_closure.py (24 tests). Counts for every (guarantee, n) pair match the expected values. A brute-force check over all C(n,15) possible draws passed for every n from 16 to 20, including n=20. Validation returns 422 as expected, no contests returns 400, and batch persistence and conferir work. The full regression suite passed 76/76 (-n 0). Frontend: modal, toggling, the 20-number limit, suggest, clear, modes, estimate, error, the disabled button, generation, the summary, the toast, history batch-options and conferir all work. Regression on the generator modal, Atraso tab and TXT export passed. No console errors.

issues: Grammar: 'Serão gerados 1 jogos.' should be singular ('Será gerado 1 jogo.')

design_issues.screen: Games history header for closure batches
issues: Header shows 'base: últimos 300 (até #300)' for closure batches. This is misleading because closures do not use statistics; consider showing 'Fechamento' in the header

action_items: Optional: fix the singular/plural grammar in closure-estimate

critical_code_review_comments: closure_games greedy is O(C(n,k)^2) for initial gain. n=20 g14 takes about 0.8s, which is acceptable. It runs synchronously in the async endpoint and blocks the event loop briefly; consider run_in_threadpool
Frontend COUNTS table is hardcoded and duplicates the backend's deterministic results. It is correct now but will drift if the algorithm changes
Existing test_lotofacil_api.py leaves some generated batches (1/10/100 games) in the DB on each run (pre-existing, minor)
seed_data_creation: None. test_no_contests_400 backs up all 300 contests, clears them, then re-uploads them. The DB still has 300 contests (#1-#300). Batches created by the UI tests were deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with -n 0. test_closure.py brute-forces the guarantee for n up to 20 (~5s total).
